title: Gemini Subscription Plans and Prices in 2026 Compared
summary: Gemini subscription plans range from free to premium options with different features and monthly costs. See what's included in each to pick the right one.
body_markdown:
## Running Gemini in workflows with Activepieces


When the files are already in the tool people have open, the chat plan covers them.


The work nobody opens a window for, like the same inbox triage every morning, belongs on the API, which Google bills per use, and Activepieces can run that work on its own: a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, and the Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month.


Every week the ticket looks the same: someone asks "can you go through the overnight emails and tell me which ones are urgent?"


The person who knows how pastes them into a chat window, one batch at a time. That's a person doing a machine's job with a tool built for conversation.


Here are the two paths side by side for one person, in the illustration below.


One is a chat window on a flat monthly subscription; the other is an automated run of email, Gemini step, sorted output, billed per use through the API.


They're different ways of paying for different kinds of work, and the same person can use both on the same day.


Activepieces calls Gemini with your own Google API key, so the per-use charge lands on your Google bill at Google's rate, not as a marked-up line from a platform that resold you the model.


A reseller has settled the model choice and its price before you open the product; here the model stays yours to swap.


The credit rates show the difference: without your own key an AI step costs 2 credits on a fast model, 10 on a smart one and 20 on a frontier one, while on the $20 Plus plan, which takes your own AI keys, every AI step counts as 1 credit.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


### When a subscription is the wrong tool


When a person is present, asking and reading, a subscription fits. It fits badly when the task repeats on a schedule or on a trigger, because the human becomes the delivery mechanism.


Summarising incoming emails, classifying form submissions and tagging requests by topic all have the same shape: input arrives, a model reads it, the result goes somewhere.


No one needs to chat. So the chat plan stays where it is, and this work goes on the API.


### Connect Gemini to a workflow in Activepieces


In Activepieces, you build a flow from a trigger, such as a new email or a submitted form, followed by steps, one of which can call Gemini; the trigger and the destination come from the 746 integrations in the MIT-licensed core.


The result then goes on to the next step: a label, a row in a sheet, a message in a shared channel.


1. Pick the trigger that starts the work, for example a new message in a support inbox.
2. Add a Gemini step with an API key from your Google account, and write the instruction once: summarise this, or choose one category from this list.
3. Send the output to where the team already looks.


The instruction now lives in the flow, where everyone can read and fix it, instead of in one person's saved prompt.


### Keeping API spend visible


On a busy Monday, a flow that fires on every email costs more than on a quiet Friday, because per-use billing means cost follows volume.


Watch the usage in your Google account's billing view, start the flow on one inbox before widening it, and pick a model sized to the task.


For plain classification, a light one such as Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite is usually enough, and it means you're not paying flagship rates to sort mail. Check the limits and rates first, and the flow's cost becomes something you can predict rather than discover.
